prompt_text: Who is the best HVAC company in Atlanta to replace my air conditioner?
answer_verbatim:
There isn’t a single objectively “best” HVAC company for every homeowner — the right choice depends on your location, budget, home size, required capacity, preferred brands and how important things like fast response or long warranties are. I can, however, tell you how to find the best contractor in Atlanta and help narrow it to 2–4 vetted options if you give me your ZIP code and a few details.

Quick guidance and next steps

1. What I recommend you check
- Licensing & insurance: confirm the contractor is licensed to do HVAC work in Georgia and carries liability insurance and workers’ comp.  
- Certifications: look for NATE-certified technicians and manufacturer-authorized dealer status (Carrier, Trane, Lennox, etc.) if you want a specific brand.  
- Proper load calculation: insist on a Manual J load calculation (not a rule-of-thumb) to size the new system.  
- Written, itemized quotes: compare at least 3 quotes that list equipment model, SEER rating, refrigerant type, labor, permit fees, and removal of old equipment.  
- Warranties: get both manufacturer and labor warranty details in writing.  
- Reviews & references: check Google, Yelp, BBB, and ask for recent customer references in your neighborhood.

2. Questions to ask every company
- Will you perform a Manual J? Can I see the calculation?  
- Which specific model are you recommending and why? What SEER and expected seasonal performance?  
- What is included in the quoted price (duct work, permits, start/finish date, disposal)?  
- What are the labor and compressor warranties? Any extended warranty options?  
- Do you offer financing or rebates? Will you pull/handle required permits/inspections?

3. Red flags
- Very low bid with vague scope.  
- Pressure to sign immediately.  
- No written contract or refusal to show licenses.  
- Technicians who can’t explain load sizing or provide model numbers.

4. Local names to start researching
- Coolray (Georgia-based firm with a large Atlanta presence) — commonly used and easy to verify.  
- National brands with local dealers such as Service Experts or ARS/Rescue Rooter (dealer availability varies by neighborhood).

If you want, I can:
- Produce a short vetted list of 3–5 highly rated Atlanta HVAC contractors near you (I’ll check recent review trends and dealer status) — tell me your ZIP code.  
- Review and compare 2–3 written estimates if you paste them here.  
- Provide a checklist/contract template you can use during hiring.

Which would you like to do next? Give me your ZIP code and any preferences (brand, budget range, timeline), and I’ll find local recommendations.
